title: Multiscale Quantum-Classical Simulation of Protein Autoproteolysis in a Million-Atom Membrane Environment
summary: arXiv:2610.23108v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Predicting chemical reactions in biomolecules is challenging because reactive centers are embedded within complex environments that strongly influence their energetics and mechanisms. Here, we present a hybrid quantum-classical workflow that combines molecular dynamics, density functional theory, and correlated wavefunction methods, tightly integrating CPUs, GPUs, and quantum processing units (QPUs) to enable simulations across multiple length and accuracy scales. summary: arXiv:2507.20130v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Recent breakthroughs in generative models have shown great promise for drug discovery, yet Structure-Based Drug Design (SBDD) faces two critical challenges: the scarcity of high-quality protein-ligand complex data and the practical synthesizability of generated molecules. While ligand-based approaches benefit from billion-scale small molecule datasets, they often lack the structural context of the target protein. title: Network organization of protein binding-site landscapes across scales
summary: Studying protein binding sites helps explain ligand recognition and selectivity, informing drug development and repurposing. Here, we combine protein language model embeddings with network analysis to investigate how local recognition environments organize across scales. We represented 121,673 non-redundant, experimentally identified binding sites using ProtT5 embeddings of ligand-contacting residues and constructed a mutual nearest-neighbor network. summary: The three-dimensional structure of proteins provides essential insight into the molecular mechanisms underlying their function. Many biological activities are mediated through protein interactions, making accurate structural determination of protein complexes important. Despite significant advances in computational protein structure prediction, there are still many cases where protein complexes are not correctly assembled. title: RiboBridge couples RNA backbone generation to sequence design through a learned interaction topology
summary: Designing ribonucleic acid (RNA) molecules with prescribed structures and functions is central to RNA engineering. Backbone-first approaches generate three-dimensional geometry before assigning a nucleotide sequence, yet leave open how that geometry should be represented for downstream sequence design. Here we introduce RiboBridge, which infers a probabilistic residue-pair state from backbone geometry, recycles binary pair probabilities through a second pass and transfers binary and typed signals as soft attention biases for sequence decoding. summary: Lasso peptides are a class of ribosomally synthesized and post-translationally modified peptides (RiPPs) characterized by a mechanically interlocked topology, in which the C-terminal tail is threaded through an N-terminal macrolactam ring formed by an isopeptide bond. This unique topology often confers high thermal stability and resistance to proteolytic degradation. title: The (implicit) force is with you: an application of the implicit function theorem for automatic protein force fields reparametrization
summary: Molecular dynamics simulations are powerful tools for studying protein behavior, yet their accuracy remains limited by the approximations of molecular force fields and the difficulty of determining their parameters. Moreover, existing force fields are largely optimized for globular proteins and can perform poorly on structurally distinct systems. summary: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent anthropogenic "forever chemicals" whose strong C-F bonds (~460-533 kJ mol-1) resist defluorination, and the recast EU Drinking Water Directive sets parametric values of 0.10 ug L-1 for the sum of 20 specified PFAS and 0.50 ug L-1 for total PFAS. title: CucurbitAgent: An AI agent for exploring cucurbit multi-omics resources
summary: Functional genomics in crops increasingly depends on integrating information from an extensive literature and heterogeneous multi-omics datasets. Large language models (LLMs) offer a powerful approach to synthesizing these resources and revealing hidden connections across datasets; however, they frequently hallucinate, producing plausible but unsupported claims, when responding to gene-specific queries. title: MYC targeted de novo binders impair tumor growth
summary: MYC is one of the most frequently dysregulated oncogenic drivers across many cancers, yet direct therapeutic targeting has remained difficult because its function is mediated by disordered regions and transient protein-protein interactions. Here we design proteins that bind epitopes within regions of MYC whose sequence is conserved between human and mouse, including intrinsically disordered motifs required for oncogenic activity. summary: Histone deacetylase 6 (HDAC6) plays an essential role in the regulation of post-translational lysine acetylation. Myriad biological processes depend on the precise regulation of lysine acetylation-deacetylation cycles, and their dysregulation is linked to human pathologies such as cancer and neurodegeneration. title: Nucleotide State Regulates Asymmetric Substrate-Binding Protein Docking in a Type II ABC Importer
summary: Type II ABC importers rely on substrate-binding proteins (SBP) to capture nutrients and deliver them to membrane-embedded transporters, but how ATP binding and hydrolysis regulate their interactions remains poorly understood. To address these questions, we determined structures of the Type II small-substrate molybdate importer MolBC-A from H. influenzae in distinct nucleotide-bound states, complemented by molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and functional assays. title: Identification and targeting of a novel drug pocket in the tumour angiogenesis regulator RhoJ
summary: The Rho GTPase RhoJ is a key regulator of tumour angiogenesis and has been identified as a target for anti-angiogenic drug design. Its high sequence conservation with the related Rho GTPase Cdc42 complicates selective drug discovery. RhoJ has a unique N-terminal extension (Asn2-Lys19) that is absent in Cdc42 and other Rho GTPases. title: Allosteric covalent inhibition of cereblon through cryptic cysteine targeting
summary: Thalidomide-derived cereblon (CRBN) modulators are among the most clinically impactful targeted protein degradation therapeutics, redirecting the CRL4-CRBN E3 ubiquitin ligase to degrade disease-driving neosubstrates. title: A potent macrocyclic peptide binder enables effector-free crystallization of the GTPase RAB27A
summary: RAB27A is a member of a highly conserved family of small GTPases that regulate intracellular vesicle trafficking. Multiple studies have linked RAB27A cellular activity to exosome-mediated modulation of the tumour microenvironment and inflammatory signalling, highlighting it as an attractive target for drug discovery. summary: The elucidation of the atomistic structure of PrPSc has, disappointingly, not revealed the mechanism underlying prion propagation.
